entries.heading: PayFast Signature Sort Bug (Critical — Revenue Impact)
entries.body: As described in the Payment section: `generateSignature()` originally called `.sort()` on the keys array. PayFast verifies using insertion order, not alphabetical order. Removing `.sort()` fixed payment failures. File: `lib/payfast/index.ts`.

entries.heading: Price Formatting /100 Bug
entries.body: Product prices are stored in the database in cents (integer). Early implementations in several components called `price.toFixed(2)` directly on the cents value, displaying R29900 instead of R299. The fix was to divide by 100 before formatting: `(price / 100).toFixed(2)`. Files fixed: `components/marketplace/ProductCoverCard.tsx`, `components/marketplace/ProductDetailClient.tsx`, `components/cart/CartItem.tsx`, `components/cart/CartDrawer.tsx`, `app/checkout/page.tsx`.

entries.heading: Brand Inconsistency — Mirembe Muse vs CreativelyNanda
entries.body: Early product copy and metadata mixed the Mirembe Muse brand (the company behind the Notion templates) with the CreativelyNanda personal brand. The resolution was clear branding separation: Mirembe Muse is the product/company brand shown on templates and the `/mirembe` landing page; CreativelyNanda is the personal brand for the portfolio, blog, and poetry. The site domain remains `creativelynanda.co.za`.

entries.heading: Resend API Key Rename
entries.body: The original environment variable `RESEND_KEY` was renamed to `RESEND_API_KEY` to match Resend's official documentation and their SDK's default lookup. All email sending was silently failing before this fix.

entries.heading: OrderItem Missing Fields Bug
entries.body: The cart store's `CartItem` type was missing `slug` and `guide_url` fields that the webhook handler needed to construct download links and Notion template URLs in the confirmation email. These fields were added to the type definition and populated at checkout time.

entries.heading: PAYFAST_SANDBOX Config Key
entries.body:
The config read `PAYFAST_SANDBOX_MODE` but the `.env.local` set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYFAST_SANDBOX`. The config was corrected to read `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYFAST_SANDBOX`, ensuring sandbox/live mode switching works correctly.

---

entries.heading: Arcjet Security Middleware
entries.body:
`middleware.ts` at the project root integrates `@arcjet/next@1.3.0` with three rule types:

- `shield({ mode: "LIVE" })` — Blocks common attack patterns
- `detectBot({ mode: "LIVE", allow: ["CATEGORY:SEARCH_ENGINE", ...] })` — Blocks malicious bots while allowing Googlebot, Bingbot, and preview bots
- `slidingWindow({ interval: "1m", max: 60 })` — 60 req/min rate limit globally, 10 req/min for AI routes

The middleware matches all routes except `_next/static`, `_next/image`, and `favicon.ico`.

entries.heading: Firebase Push Notifications
entries.body: `lib/firebase-messaging.ts` implements lazy-loading Firebase Cloud Messaging. The module only imports Firebase in the browser (`typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard). Three exported functions: `subscribeToNotifications()` (requests permission, returns FCM token), `onForegroundMessage()` (registers a callback for foreground push payloads), and `getMessaging()` (internal lazy initialiser). The service worker at `public/firebase-messaging-sw.js` handles background push. All Firebase config values use `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*` environment variables.

entries.heading: Vercel Analytics
entries.body: `<Analytics />` from `@vercel/analytics/next` is included in `app/layout.js`. This provides automatic page view tracking and Web Vitals reporting without any configuration.

entries.heading: Google Tag Manager
entries.body: GTM (`NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID=GTM-5ZMQ7H4M`) is loaded conditionally in the root layout. GTM allows adding additional tags (GA4, Hotjar, custom events) without code deployments.

entries.heading: PostHog
entries.body: `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` (previously incorrectly named `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`) provides product analytics. PostHog's session recording and funnel analysis helps understand where users drop off in the checkout flow.

entries.heading: Hotjar and Crisp
entries.body: Hotjar (`NEXT_PUBLIC_HOTJAR_ID`) provides heatmaps and session recordings. Crisp (`NEXT_PUBLIC_CRISP_WEBSITE_ID`) provides live chat. Both are loaded conditionally in the root layout — they only initialise when the environment variable is present, making local development cleaner.

entries.heading: Schema.org @graph in Root Layout
entries.body:
The root layout renders a single `application/ld+json` script containing a `@graph` array with `WebSite` and `Person` structured data. This is the recommended pattern for personal brand sites — Google can understand the site's identity from a single structured data block on every page.

entries.heading: Overview
entries.body:
Before 7 live SaaS applications. Before POPIA registration. Before 400+ GitHub commits and a registered South African technology company. There were these projects.

The foundation projects documented here represent the deliberate education of a Creative Technologist who started with zero formal programming background in mid-2025 and reached full-stack AI engineering capability by March 2026. Each project was a targeted lesson. Each lesson was kept.

This document is not a portfolio showcase — it is a build chronicle. It answers the question that fellowship applications, technical interviews, and client proposals all eventually ask: *"Where did you learn to build?"*

The answer is here.
 https://women-retreat-yellowwood-forest.vercel.app/ https://green-valut-e-commerce-store-demo.vercel.app/ https://poetry-tube.vercel.app/ https://kustom-krafts.vercel.app/ https://cortex-hub-booking-5e35.vercel.app/ https://true-access-app.vercel.app/
---

entries.heading: The Learning Architecture
entries.body:
The foundation projects were not random. They were sequenced to build competency in layers:

**Layer 1 — HTML/CSS/Vanilla JS:** Static sites and presentational projects (Retreat, Carpentry, Weather App)  
**Layer 2 — API Integration:** Working with external data sources, state management, async patterns (Weather App, YouTube Clone)  
**Layer 3 — Full-Stack with Database:** Auth, data persistence, multi-role systems (Cortex Hub, GreenVault)  
**Layer 4 — Real-Time & Payments:** WebSockets, payment gateways, webhook handling (GreenVault, PoetryTube)  
**Layer 5 — Co-Founder / Product Thinking:** Mapbox, complex data architecture, social impact (TrueAccApp)  
**Layer 6 — Client Work:** Real briefs, real clients, real delivery (Retreat, Carpentry, Chanty)

Each layer built directly on the last. The sequence was not accidental.

---

entries.heading: The Throughline
entries.body:
Across all foundation projects, nine principles were established that now govern every build in the Mirembe Muse portfolio:

1. **Emotional architecture before technical implementation** — what should the user feel first; what enables that feeling second
2. **WhatsApp is the SA UX pattern** — integrate or be irrelevant for the local market
3. **PayFast ITN is the foundation of SA commerce** — learn it once, deploy it everywhere
4. **Database primitives before application code** — solve problems in PostgreSQL when possible
5. **Zero dependencies is a feature for the right context** — not everything needs React
6. **Client work seeds product ideas** — every manual SME process is a future SaaS feature
7. **Clone to learn, not to copy** — reverse-engineer what exists to understand what to build instead
8. **Accessibility is a quality standard, not a feature** — WCAG compliance makes products better for everyone
9. **The personal project is the most differentiated** — biographical legitimacy cannot be engineered

These nine principles are the intellectual property that no GitHub repository can fully contain. They live in the decisions made on every line of code written since.

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: A wellness retreat operator in the Eastern Cape needed a digital presence that could do what a personal recommendation does: make a potential guest feel safe before she had met anyone. The target audience was women who would not book anything they could not trust.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
The project began with the emotional destination — *what should a visitor feel 10 seconds after landing?* — and worked backwards to the technical implementation. The answer was: held. Calm. Like arriving somewhere that was made for her.

That feeling required a specific combination of technical decisions: full-bleed nature photography served with optimal loading, layered typography using a serif display font that slows the reader down, a narrative content sequence that answers emotional questions before practical ones, and zero visual clutter that might break the spell.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**Design is an argument.** Every visual decision argues for something — usually about the relationship between the brand and the visitor. The retreat's design argued: *"We see you. This is safe. You belong here."* Making that argument required understanding the audience's psychology before touching the keyboard.

This was also the first lesson in the gap between a technically correct website and an emotionally effective one. Both render in the browser. Only one converts.

entries.heading: Deliverable Quality
entries.body:
The site launched on schedule and was used actively for retreat promotion. It established the standard for all subsequent client work: emotional architecture first, technical implementation second.

---

entries.heading: Trade Services Web Experience | Client Work
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [kustom-krafts](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/kustom-krafts) *(carpentry business, title updated)*  
**Stack:** HTML5 · CSS3 · Vanilla JavaScript  
**Type:** Client Work

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: A South African carpentry and joinery business with genuine craft and zero digital presence. All business via word-of-mouth. The brief: build something that looks serious enough to justify serious prices.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
The first decision was the most important: the portfolio gallery goes above the fold. Not the pitch, not the pricing — the work. In the trades market, the product sells itself if you can see it. The entire design hierarchy flows from that conviction.

The technical challenge was image performance. A gallery-heavy site on a static HTML/CSS build needed careful optimisation: aspect ratio locks to prevent layout shift, lazy loading via native browser APIs, and WebP image format recommendations for the client's photography workflow.

The WhatsApp CTA integration was the conversion insight. South African clients in the SME market communicate via WhatsApp as a default. A contact form alone loses leads. A WhatsApp deep link — `wa.me/27XXXXXXXXX?text=Hi, I saw your website...` — converts them immediately by meeting them where they already are.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**WhatsApp is the South African UX pattern.** Every subsequent product built for the SA market — AdminOS, StokvelOS, VarsityOS — has WhatsApp integration built in. This project is where that conviction was formed.

The second lesson: **zero dependencies is a feature for the right client.** A carpentry business owner cannot maintain a React application. A static HTML/CSS site that works flawlessly for 5 years without intervention is a better client outcome than a technically impressive build that breaks the moment a dependency updates.

---

entries.heading: Transport Business Web Presence | Client Work
entries.body:
**GitHub:** Prototype  
**Stack:** HTML5 · CSS3 · Vanilla JavaScript  
**Type:** Client Work | R34,000 Growth Package delivered

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: Chanty Shuttle Services: a real transport operator with reliable vehicles, quality service, and zero digital presence. The full engagement brief spanned a Growth Package (Tier 2) and a planned Vision Package (Tier 3) — the first multi-tiered client service model.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
The Growth Package deliverables were scoped as a complete digital foundation: professional website with booking inquiry flow, Google Business Profile setup, social media templates, WhatsApp Business integration, and local SEO. The Vision Package roadmap included booking automation, an affiliate/referral marketing system, and monthly performance reporting.

The affiliate marketing architecture was the intellectual breakthrough: Chanty's existing corporate clients and hotel partners could become passive referral sources if the incentive structure was right. A simple referral link system — track, attribute, reward — turns happy clients into a distribution channel. This thinking would later become a planned feature of the LemonSqueezy affiliate programme for digital products.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**Tiered pricing is a product design problem.** The Growth → Vision Package structure solved the SA SME budget reality: businesses want comprehensive digital services but cannot always afford everything at once. Tiered packages let clients start where they are and grow. This model is now standard across all client service offerings.

**Client work seeds product ideas.** The Chanty engagement crystallised a question that became AdminOS: *why is every SME owner manually managing communication, bookings, invoicing, and staff on WhatsApp?* The answer was the absence of affordable, SA-appropriate tooling. AdminOS is the productised, scaled answer to that question.

entries.heading: Commercial Outcome
entries.body:
**R34,000** Growth Package delivered. Year 1 total potential: **R88,000** with Vision Package activation. First demonstration of the Mirembe Muse B2B commercial model.

---

entries.heading: Location-Based Accessibility Platform | Co-Founder Project
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [TrueAccApp](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/TrueAccApp)  
**Stack:** Next.js · TypeScript · Mapbox GL JS · Supabase · Tailwind CSS  
**Type:** Co-Founder | Social Impact | Innovation

---

entries.heading: The Brief`
entries.body: 4 million South Africans live with disabilities. There is no comprehensive, community-verified accessibility database for South African public spaces. TrueAccApp was built to create one.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
TrueAccApp introduced four technical capabilities that had not been engaged before: Mapbox GL JS for complex spatial data visualisation, co-founder collaboration on technical architecture, crowdsourced data models with contribution validation, and WCAG accessibility compliance as a primary engineering constraint (not a retrofit).

The Mapbox integration required learning vector tile styling, custom layer management, and the difference between client-side and source filtering at the map level. The community contribution model required a Supabase schema that tracked not just location data but the confidence level of that data — how many contributors had verified it, when it was last updated, and whether it had been flagged as inaccurate.

The accessibility-first development constraint was the most important thing this project taught. Building for users with visual impairments, motor limitations, and cognitive differences requires decisions that make the product better for every user — semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, readable contrast ratios. These are not accessibility features. They are quality standards.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**Constraints produce better design.** The accessibility-first constraint on TrueAccApp produced a cleaner, more navigable interface than would have emerged from unconstrained design. Every subsequent project in the portfolio applies this principle.

**Co-founding requires explicit alignment.** The co-founder dynamic introduced a different kind of problem set: prioritisation, scope, decision authority, and the governance of shared technical decisions. Managing this gracefully while maintaining velocity was a leadership lesson that no solo build can teach.

entries.heading: Social Impact Framing
entries.body:
TrueAccApp is not a portfolio project in the traditional sense. It is civic infrastructure. The data it generates belongs to the community that contributed it. This is Ubuntu applied to product design: the platform exists because the community needs it, and the community makes it more valuable by using it.

---

entries.heading: Weather × Poetry × Self-Care | Creative Personal Project
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [my-weather-app](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/my-weather-app)  
**Stack:** HTML5 · CSS3 · Vanilla JavaScript · OpenWeatherMap API  
**Type:** Personal / Creative / Technical Study

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: Every developer who has completed an introductory JavaScript course has built a weather app. The question was: *what does a weather app built by a published poet look like?*

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
The technical implementation — API key, geolocation, fetch, parse, render — was the fastest part of the build. The real work was the content library: original poems written for each weather condition (rain, clear, clouds, wind, storm), self-care rituals matched to each condition, and a South Africa-specific addition that no tutorial suggests — the load shedding mood card.

The load shedding card is the most-shared element in user testing. It is also the most honest. A weather app for South African users that pretends Eskom doesn't exist has already failed its audience. The card pairs load shedding with candle rituals, battery-saving affirmations, and a poem about sitting in the dark. It converts what is universally acknowledged as a frustration into a moment of care. That is the MoodCast product philosophy applied.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**The standard project is the starting point, not the destination.** Every tutorial project in the curriculum was approached as a brief: what would this look like if it was actually good? What would make this memorable? The weather app became MoodCast. The YouTube clone became the research document for WatchSankofa. The eCommerce demo became GreenVault. The question *"what would make this mine?"* is the design process.

**The SA load shedding card is a product insight, not a joke.** Products that acknowledge the lived reality of their users' context earn trust that technically superior competitors without that awareness cannot buy.

---

entries.heading: Smart Workspace Booking Platform | Full-Stack SaaS Prototype
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [Cortex-Hub-Booking](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/Cortex-Hub-Booking)  
**Stack:** Next.js · TypeScript · Supabase · PayFast · Resend · Tailwind CSS  
**Type:** SaaS Prototype | Full-Stack Study

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: Shared workspaces and creative hubs in South Africa are managed via WhatsApp and paper booking registers. Double bookings happen. Revenue leaks. No-shows go unmanaged. A real booking system exists for hotels and airlines — why not for creative hubs?

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
Cortex Hub Booking was the first full-stack project with a complete commercial data model: spaces, bookings, members, payments, and availability logic. The availability check — the deceptively simple question of "is this space free?" — was the most technically demanding problem in the portfolio to that point.

The solution required understanding PostgreSQL's `tsrange` data type and its overlap operator (`&&`). A booking conflict check is not a simple equality comparison — it's an interval overlap problem that must handle partial overlaps (a booking that starts before the requested time and ends during it), concurrent bookings submitted simultaneously, and the difference between a soft hold and a confirmed reservation. Solving this at the database level with a constraint rather than in application code was the architectural insight.

PayFast integration introduced webhook handling for the first time. The ITN (Instant Transaction Notification) signature verification pattern — URL-encoding parameters in a specific sequence, appending the passphrase, and MD5-hashing the result — is now used across every PayFast integration in the portfolio: GreenVault, VarsityOS, StokvelOS, AdminOS.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**Database primitives first, application code second.** Every problem that can be solved in the database should be. Availability checking, uniqueness constraints, concurrent booking prevention — these belong in PostgreSQL, not in Next.js server actions. This principle guides the Supabase architecture across all seven SaaS applications.

**Booking systems become AdminOS.** After building Cortex Hub, the pattern was unmistakable: South African SMEs don't need individual point solutions — they need an operating layer that handles communication, bookings, invoicing, staff management, and analytics as an integrated whole. AdminOS is the answer to the question Cortex Hub asked.

---

entries.heading: Video Platform Architecture Study | Foundation for WatchSankofa
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [CreativelyNanda-Youtube-clone](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/CreativelyNanda-Youtube-clone)  
**Stack:** HTML5 · CSS3 · Vanilla JavaScript  
**Built:** July 13, 2025 — the very beginning  
**Type:** Technical Foundation Study | UI Reverse Engineering

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body:
Before building WatchSankofa — an African-first streaming platform — it was necessary to deeply understand the product being improved upon. The YouTube clone was not a tutorial exercise. It was a UI reverse-engineering session conducted with a specific question in mind: *what does YouTube get wrong for African creators?*

And it was done in pure HTML and CSS. No React. No API. No framework.

entries.heading: What Was Built
entries.body:
Running locally on July 13, 2025, the clone reproduced YouTube's full interface from scratch: the sidebar navigation with icons and labels, the top nav with search bar and icons, and a 4-column video card grid with custom-designed thumbnails. Every thumbnail was branded as `@CreativelyNanda` — a poetry short film, a web dev study plan, a lookbook, a build-in-public vlog. The view counts and timestamps were written by hand. The channel name was already there.

This was day one. This is where the empire started.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**Fundamentals before frameworks.** The developer who can build YouTube's UI in raw CSS understands the web. Understanding YouTube's layout at the CSS level — every grid column, every positioned badge, every hover state — is what makes WatchSankofa's design decisions deliberate. The clone is the research. The thumbnails are the autobiography.

**The content told the story before the company existed.** Eight custom thumbnails: a poetry performance, a coding journey, a personal essay on identity, a style lookbook. In July 2025, Nanda had not yet started building SaaS apps. But the thumbnails already knew who she was going to become.

---

entries.heading: Sustainable Commerce Platform | Full-Stack eCommerce Architecture
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [GreenValut-eCommerce-store-demo](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/GreenValut-eCommerce-store-demo)  
**Stack:** Next.js · TypeScript · Supabase · PayFast · Resend · Tailwind CSS  
**Type:** Full-Stack Demo | eCommerce Architecture

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body: South African sustainable products — natural hair care, organic food, ethical textiles — are scattered and underrepresented digitally. GreenVault was built to demonstrate what a curated, values-aligned African eco-commerce platform could look like, and to solve the full technical stack of eCommerce: catalogue, cart, checkout, payment, digital goods delivery.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
GreenVault was the most technically comprehensive foundation project. The eCommerce data model — products, categories, cart sessions, orders, order items, reviews, digital downloads — required planning relational integrity that would survive real-world usage patterns: concurrent carts, failed payments, partial refunds, digital goods expiry.

The digital goods delivery flow was the most technically interesting component. PayFast sends an Instant Transaction Notification (ITN) to a webhook endpoint when payment is confirmed. That webhook must validate the ITN signature, update the order status, generate a signed Supabase Storage URL with a 48-hour expiry, and trigger the confirmation email via Resend — all in a single atomic server action. Getting that chain right was the most satisfying technical moment in the foundation projects.

The earth-toned design system — forest green, terracotta, cream, warm amber — validated that the Mirembe Muse colour palette is inherently a sustainable commerce palette. GreenVault's visual identity became the design template for the Mirembe Muse Store.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**PayFast ITN handling is the foundation of SA eCommerce.** The signature verification pattern, the webhook idempotency requirement (the same ITN can arrive multiple times — the handler must be safe to run repeatedly), and the async email dispatch architecture are now standard across every payment-enabled product in the portfolio.

**eCommerce architecture scales to SaaS.** The multi-role patterns (guest vs. authenticated user vs. admin), the order state machine (pending → confirmed → fulfilled → refunded), and the signed URL delivery system all reappear in the SaaS product architecture. Building them in GreenVault first meant they were production-tested before being deployed at scale.

---

entries.heading: Video Platform for Poets | Creative Community Technology
entries.body:
**GitHub:** [PoetryTube](https://github.com/Nanda-Regine/PoetryTube)  
**Stack:** Next.js · TypeScript · Supabase · Mux · Tailwind CSS  
**Type:** Community Platform | Creative Technology | Personal Mission

---

entries.heading: The Brief
entries.body:
YouTube has no concept of spoken word poetry as a distinct cultural form. The algorithm that recommends videos has no understanding of what makes a great slam performance, no ability to surface voices performing in isiZulu or Luganda to audiences who speak those languages, and no incentive to care. Poets who build audiences on YouTube are succeeding despite the platform, not because of it.

PoetryTube was built because this is personal. *Inside Her Roses* exists. The performances exist. The injustice of the algorithmic invisibility exists.

entries.heading: The Build
entries.body:
The live applause feature was the hardest and most important technical problem in the foundation projects. Supabase Realtime's presence and broadcast channels enable it: when a viewer taps applause during a performance, a broadcast is sent to all connected clients on that performance. The counter increments in real time for everyone watching simultaneously. That shared moment — the digital equivalent of a room filling with applause — changes the experience of watching a performance from asynchronous media consumption to live cultural event.

The language-first content architecture required a tagging system that treated language as a discovery dimension equal to category or theme. Search and recommendation filters built around language affinity produce results that feel culturally accurate rather than algorithmically generic.

entries.heading: The Lesson
entries.body:
**The most personal project is the most differentiated.** PoetryTube is technically complex — real-time systems, video processing, community architecture. But the technical complexity is not what makes it stand out. What makes it stand out is that it was built by a published poet who has lived the exact problem it solves. That biographical legitimacy cannot be engineered. It can only be honoured.

**Products built from injustice last.** MoodCast was built from curiosity. GreenVault was built from a market gap. PoetryTube was built from frustration at a structural wrong. The best products come from the third motivation.

---

entries.session: CONTENT LIBRARY REBUILD — diagnosis, engine fixes, brand re-map (Aug 7 2026)
entries.heading: CONTENT LIBRARY REBUILD — diagnosis, engine fixes, brand re-map (Aug 7 2026)
entries.ownerQuote: clean current visuals first or we pile up posts that aren't working
entries.body:
**Build gate:** NO tsc (crashes the laptop) — esbuild per-file + tsx + **every layout change verified by rendering the real PNG and looking at it.** 4 commits + docs, pushed to master.

**Context.** Returned after building on another device — synced 544 commits (fast-forward stalled on OneDrive's 1,590-file checkout + a stale `index.lock`; recovered with `reset --hard origin/master`). Studied the full journey + mapped the live code with three parallel agents (arch/infra, wings/routes, data model). The code had drifted well ahead of the docs.

**Docs re-grounded to reality.** `CLAUDE.md` (root + global `~/.claude`) referenced modules that don't exist (`agents.ts`, `agents.config.ts`, `get-jarvis-user.ts`) and wrong model IDs. Corrected against verified source: real model IDs (`sonnet-4-6`/`haiku-4-5-20251001`/`opus-4-8`, Opus = Autobiography only), real module paths (`get-user.ts`, `anthropic.ts`, `notionClient()`, `redis/client.ts`), the hard-won laws (getJarvisUser is a data accessor NOT an auth gate; the Redis footgun; waitUntil not bare void), 15→27 wings, and the **tsc-is-banned build gate**. Also documented **Marketing (owner) vs Studio (team) are NOT duplicates** so no future session merges them.

**The library diagnosis (owner: "clean current visuals first or we pile up posts that aren't working").** Live SQL on `marketing_assets`: **382 live assets, 0 previewed/approved** (the entire vault stuck behind the preview gate), **only 9 linked to a post** (373 orphaned), **79 flagged clipped**, only two types present (carousels 4:5 + a few reels 9:16). `brand_posts` had 2–4 posts/brand with messy `post_type` and no visual briefs — captions and visuals are two disconnected worlds.

**Engine fix 1 — phone mockups (commit 16197351).** The phone frame is a right-aligned portrait bleeding off the well; in 4:5 the module stacked full-width, leaving the whole left of the well empty with the words dumped below. Now a phone module (`:has(.devph)`) lays out **words-panel left / handset right** in 4:5 + 9:16 (matching 16:9); display type scaled for the narrower panel; handset sized by width so the bezel stays intact. Verified by render.

**Engine fix 2 — cover/CTA deck clamp (commit dc9d1828).** ~68 of the 79 clipped were the deck clamped to 3 lines on cover/CTA cards while a large plate/QR sat empty below. Widened the 4:5 deck to 5 lines on a wider measure + CTA headline to 4 lines. Verified: a real 185-char nanda cover deck + a cut CTA headline now render `ok:true`, full copy, room to spare.

**Brand re-map to Nanda's real architecture (commit 1e87a335).** The code had the founder brands reversed. Corrected: **nanda_personal (@nanda.regine) = the POETRY OASIS** (writers'/poets' home — craft tips, exercises, poems, story snippets; stories funnel to Wattpad/WritersCafe; no site, no logo → typographic wordmark). **creativelynanda (CN) = the ENGINEER/FOUNDER room** (engineer/founder/systems-architect, build-in-public + ray.so code cards; creativelynanda.co.za, real logo). **Mirembe = the firm** (authority, not app screenshots). routeFunnel rebuilt to three rooms (poetry→oasis, engineer/founder→CN, studio→Mirembe); NATIVE_INTENT + BRAND_ROLES updated. TODO: real Wattpad/WritersCafe URLs (placeholders flagged).

**The plan agreed (memory `project-content-library-rebuild`).** Content types = Carousel · Reel · Statement/Quote · Single image · Long-form · **Code card (ray.so)** — every brand gets ALL of them, with depth. Platform lanes: auto (Hashnode/Dev.to/Meta/Twitter/LinkedIn) + manual copy-paste (Substack/Medium/WritersCafe/Wattpad). Cadence: **5×/week min** (~60 pieces/brand Aug→Oct). Reels music: hero → draft + trending audio in-app; volume → embedded royalty-free bed. Covers get a hero logo lockup (real logos for the 5 that have them; CN pending; nanda.regine wordmark). Next: finalise cover template → **bulk re-render all 382 clean** → taxonomy/set model → build the missing type generators (copy gen runs on Vercel — Anthropic key is not local) → rebuild the Vault as brand→type→set → wire scheduling/publishing day one. Best marketing/sales/algorithm practice baked into every generator (hooks, save/share triggers, single CTAs, SEO-weighted long-form).

The theme: great backend code the UI was hiding. Four audit agents mapped it; then fixed.

Routed it all through `ChatMarkdown` — Board of Advisors (synthesis/recommendation/deliberations), Speech Factory, CEO chat, North-Star, Dossiers, and Scholar's law answers / Africa entries / language tutor. Fixed the shared root cause of the curriculum cut-off too: `ChatMarkdown`'s code blocks used `overflow-x-auto` and clipped mis-fenced prose — now they wrap and scroll vertically.
- **Scholar layout bugs**: the "velocity" stat tile overflowed its cell (min-w-0 + truncate + tabular-nums); the Art Emergence "fragments/wk" pill spilled out of its oval on mobile (flex-shrink-0 + nowrap + header wrap).
- **Body reframed to reality**: she has no smartwatch and can't know exact micronutrients, so the fantasy-precision inputs are gone. Breathwork's "Pre/Post HRV (ms)" → "Calm before/after (1–5)"; Recovery's "HRV (ms)" log → an "Energy (1–10)" check-in; the home subtitle/empty-states dropped HRV. Nutrition macros are now explicitly optional ballpark ("don't stress exact numbers"), and the Supplements page stopped inventing "+Xmg iron · +N micronutrients" — it shows what each supplement is *for* instead.

Deferred (need a canonical-choice decision): the Recovery-Hub vs Nervous-System duplicate pages, a few other scholar/body duplications, Scholar's scope drift (Product Studio / Composer really belong to Marketing), and the full qualitative-nutrition rework (touches the API).

entries.heading: Engineering revamp — Installments 10-11: CTO-gap closure + real 70% project-start (July 22 2026)
entries.body:
**Build gate:** esbuild — all changed files parse clean. Commits `4caf099` (gaps 1-3) + `abdeceb` (70% start). Detail: [[project-engineering-revamp]].

Closed the three gaps a big-tech CTO would name, then made the "start a new build 70% done" loop real:

- **Push alerting (Discord + in-app).** New `src/lib/engineering/alerting.ts` — `pushOpsAlert()` fans one event to the in-app notification centre AND the Discord ops webhook (colour-coded embeds), best-effort. Wired into the health-check worker so a **new** down/degraded incident (transition-based, reusing the existing dedup — no repeat spam) and its recovery both push to you; plus an aggregated critical-CVE push from the dependency scanner. Health that finds *you* instead of waiting to be looked at.
- **SLOs with error budgets.** Readiness now computes a 30-day uptime SLO per app from `app_slo_daily` against the app's client target (`monitoring_clients.sla_target_pct`, else 99.5%) as an "Error budget (30d SLO)" check that fails when the budget is spent. Thresholds moved into a `ReadinessPolicy` object so they're tunable, not hardcoded.
- **CI / code health.** New `engineering/ci-status` worker (2h cron) pulls the latest GitHub Actions run on each app's default branch → caches it in Redis → a "CI pipeline" readiness check. The scorecard now covers *code* health, not just runtime — 12 objective checks total.
- **The 70% project start, wired end-to-end.** The harvester (walks ≤30 of your GitHub repos, AI-extracts reusable patterns into `golden_bricks`) and the service-scaffold catalog existed but had no UI on-ramp. Added a **"⛏ Harvest from repos"** button on the Bricks page, and made each Service Starter show the *actual* golden bricks from your library that slot into it (matched by `recommendedBrickTags`, with a count) — links to Harvest when empty. Pick a starter (the 30% base) + your harvested bricks (the reusable 70%) = a new project mostly built from code you've already shipped.

entries.heading: Engineering revamp — Installments 7-8: full-dashboard audit + fixes + built the dead Intel feed (July 22 2026)
entries.body:
**Build gate:** esbuild — all changed files parse clean. Commits `89cf0a2` (fixes) + `627b206` (tech-feed). Detail: [[project-engineering-revamp]].

Ran a 4-way parallel audit of every Engineering page + its API route (hunting hardcoded data, broken endpoints, and response-shape mismatches), then fixed everything real:

- **Projects list was permanently empty** — the page read `j.data.items` but the route returned `data.projects`. Route now returns `items` (+ the `critical` stat the tiles needed). List + Total + Critical all populate.
- **Vercel card was blank in the default state** — the cached branch (taken whenever `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` is unset, i.e. the norm) returned rows keyed `state`/`url`, but the page reads `latest_state`/`latest_url`, and returned up to 50 rows → duplicate React keys. Now deduped to latest-per-app and mapped to the live-path shape.
- **Workflow worker** — "tasks done" always read 0 (filtered `.eq('column','done')` but the column is `task_column`); churn hotspots could never populate (`fileChanges` was written nowhere). Fixed the column and now tally changed files from each commit's detail (bounded 25/repo to stay in GitHub's budget).
- **Honesty fixes** — root Infrastructure grid faked a pulsing green "Operational" dot for every external provider regardless of status (→ honest "Status page ↗" link); the dojo intel chip rendered a non-existent `category` field (→ `source`); the advertised `B → Golden Bricks` shortcut was a no-op (→ wired); multi-repo faked "2" repos when empty (→ real count) and had a static footer claim (→ derived); Tech Radar rendered the quadrant as a raw slug (→ human label); the Vault audit trail keyed action colours `emergency`/`access` but the writer emits `emergency_rotate`/`reveal` (emergency rotations now show red).
- **Surfaced the orphaned service-scaffold catalog** — `/api/engineering/scaffolds` (a real per-service-type starter library with files/env/first-steps) had zero UI. Now a "Service Starters" section on the Scaffold page.
- **Built the Dojo "Tech Intel" feed — it was a dead tab.** It read `engineering_tech_feed` but *nothing anywhere wrote it*, and the empty-state advertised a 06:00 cron that didn't exist. New worker `src/inngest/engineering/tech-feed.ts` (cron 06:00 SAST + `engineering/tech-feed.fetch` event) pulls Hacker News + Vercel + Supabase + Anthropic + TechCabal, Haiku-scores each item 1-10 for her stack (keyword fallback), dedupes by URL, inserts, prunes >21d. Writes `relevance` (1-10, what the Dojo filters/sorts) and source keys that match the page's `SOURCE_CFG` styling; security items get retagged `security`. Registered in `inngest/index` + `EVENTS.ENGINEERING_TECH_FEED`. Dojo POST accepts `{action:'refresh-feed'}`; the Intel tab gained a "↻ Refresh feed" button + honest empty-state copy.

Audit verdict: everything else is genuinely data-backed with honest empty states (apps/clients/architecture/tech-radar/evolution/bricks/vault/flags/security/postmortems/chat + all root cards). Known-open, low-value: apps "Three Gates"/last_deploy have no writer yet (aspirational), a redundant bottom nav on root, per-app Sentry SDK (external repos), SLA view pending real `app_slo_daily` data.

- **Lib** (`src/lib/os/weather.ts`): Open-Meteo fetch, WMO code→label, berg-wind heuristic (hot+dry+NW offshore for EL coast), `deriveWeatherInsights()` pure correlation (berg-wind HRV gap, rain↔energy, most-creative-season) — only emits with ≥3 samples per side. **10 unit tests, all pass.** Fixed a date round-trip bug (use `en-CA` for SAST YYYY-MM-DD).
- **Cron** `os/weather-memory` (21:00 SAST): fetch + snapshot + upsert + Notion sync. Registered in inngest/index.
- **API** `/api/os/weather` (GET log + insights; POST log today on demand).
- **UI** `/dashboard/os/weather` (insights cards + daily record with weather + life snapshot), dashboard quick-link.
- **Notion** DB "JarvisOS — Weather Memory" created at workspace root.

entries.session: Integration smoke-tests for new API routes (2026-06-20)
entries.heading: Integration smoke-tests for new API routes (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Closes the "tests are pure-unit only" gap for this session's routes.

- `tests/smoke/api-routes.smoke.test.ts` — exercises the REAL route handlers (not
  just libs) at two levels:
  - **Contract** (9 routes): each module loads + exports the expected HTTP methods
    as functions + `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. Catches broken imports, syntax
    errors, top-level throws, removed handlers.
  - **Request** (10 cases): invokes handlers on validation/error paths that
    short-circuit before any Supabase/Anthropic call — confirms auth wiring, body
    parsing, zod validation, invalid-JSON handling, and {error} envelopes/status
    (422/400). Boundaries stubbed like the rest of the suite: dummy Supabase env,
    redis singleton monkey-patched, global.fetch guarded.
- Added `test:smoke` npm script. Runs inside `npm test` (file ends `.test.ts`).

entries.heading: Happy-path integration smoke-tests (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Fully closes the integration-test gap: runs route handlers end-to-end with the
network boundary faked.

- `tests/smoke/api-happy-path.smoke.test.ts` — one `global.fetch` router stands
  in for Supabase PostgREST (/rest/v1: list/single/insert/count via Accept +
  method), Anthropic Messages, Open-Meteo, and ntfy. Redis monkey-patched.
- 5 success-path tests: hub GET (LCL+energy+temporal pulse), nudges GET
  (buildNudges), pronunciation POST (similarity 100 + Haiku + insert → 201),
  weather POST (Open-Meteo + insert → 201), adversarial POST (full LCL +
  constitution + Sonnet JSON + insert → 201 with a real verdict).

entries.body:

  fall back to Haiku, so it works with no key.
- **Quick Capture** (`src/lib/os/capture.ts`): pure `parseClassification` (validates
  wing/type, defaults everything) + `routeTarget` (task→todos, else→scholar_fragments)

  Web-Speech voice) is classified and **auto-filed** into the right wing.
- **DB:** `os_captures` (inbox + routing audit: raw_text, source, classified_wing/
  type, via, routed_to_table/id).
- **API** `/api/os/capture` (POST classify+route+store; GET inbox). Downstream insert
  is best-effort/guarded — a capture never fails because of routing.
- **UI** `/dashboard/os/capture` — composer with 🎙 Web-Speech voice, shows where each
  thought routed (wing + table + via model). Hub (Intelligence) + dashboard links.
- 17 unit tests (capture parse/route + groq gating). Smoke: contract + validation +

entries.body:

only, so NO existing wing routes were touched.

- **Nudge engine** (`src/lib/os/nudges.ts`) extended with 4 cross-system rules:

  os_generational_projections, scholar_readwise_highlights) — tolerant, no wing edits.

  system (or nudge) can say "argue against THIS" in one tap.

entries.heading: Phase 32 — Air Quality intelligence (2026-06-20)

entries.heading: Phase 33 — OS Hub surfaces nudges (2026-06-20)

The command surface now shows what needs you. `/dashboard/os` fetches `/api/os/nudges`
alongside the pulse and renders a tone-coloured "Needs you" strip (each links into the
relevant wing). All the proactive intelligence built this session is now visible on the
OS hub, not just inside the Goddess. Read-side, reuses the existing nudges API.

entries.heading: Phase 34 — Research Backing (Semantic Scholar) (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Find the academic papers behind a practice and save them into the Scholar library,
where they embed into Corpus (same pipeline as Readwise). Free, no key required
(optional SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY raises the rate limit).

- **Lib** (`src/lib/scholar/research.ts`): `searchSemanticScholar` (optional key
  header) + pure `normalizePaper` / `formatAuthors` / `paperToFragment` (→
  fragment_type 'reference', source 'semantic_scholar'). **5 unit tests.**
- **DB:** `scholar_research_papers` — saved library, dedupe (user_id, paper_id),
  links to the Corpus fragment.
- **API** `/api/scholar/research` (GET ?q live search w/ saved-flag, GET library,
  POST save → fragment → SCHOLAR_FRAGMENT_EMBED, DELETE). 23505 → friendly "already".
- **UI** `/dashboard/scholar/research` — search box + suggested topics, result cards
  (authors/year/citations/abstract/links), "+ Save to Corpus", research library.
  Dashboard footer + Scholar/Readwise/Corpus links.
- Smoke: contract + validation + live-search happy-path + save happy-path (S2 fetch-fake).

entries.heading: Phase 35 — Cal.com booking (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Client scheduling for the Consulting wing: bookings flow into the OS, and a
confirmed booking auto-generates a pre-call discovery brief. Env-gated on
CALCOM_API_KEY (dormant without it).

- **Lib** (`src/lib/consulting/calcom.ts`): env-gated `fetchCalcomBookings` + pure
  `normalizeBooking` / `parseWebhookBooking` (only booking-created/rescheduled) /
  `firstAttendee`. **8 unit tests.**
- **DB:** `consulting_bookings` (dedupe by user_id+calcom_id, holds the discovery brief).
- **Sync** (`calcom-sync.ts`): `ingestBooking` (idempotent upsert) + `syncCalcomBookings`
  + `generateDiscoveryBrief` (Haiku, best-effort).
- **API** `/api/consulting/calcom` (GET status+upcoming/past; POST sync — graceful disabled).
- **Webhook** `/api/webhooks/calcom` (BOOKING_CREATED → ingest + discovery brief;
  optional CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET gate).
- **Cron** `consulting/calcom-sync` (06:00 SAST, backstop). Registered.
- **UI** `/dashboard/consulting/bookings` (connected/dormant, Sync, upcoming/past with
  expandable discovery brief).
- Smoke: contract + disabled + ignore-non-booking + sync + webhook happy-paths (Cal.com fetch-fake).

entries.heading: Phase 36 — arXiv preprints in Research (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Adds arXiv as a second free research source (no key), complementing Semantic
Scholar with preprints (ML/AI, quant, sports science). Reuses the Phase 34 save→
Corpus flow and table — no new DB.

- **Lib** (`src/lib/scholar/arxiv.ts`): `searchArxiv` (no key) + pure `parseArxivFeed`
  — robust Atom-XML parsing (entity decode, whitespace collapse, optional pdf link,
  paper_id `arxiv:<id>`). **3 unit tests** incl. malformed-feed handling.
- **API:** `/api/scholar/research?source=arxiv` routes to arXiv; default = Semantic Scholar.
- **UI:** source toggle (Semantic Scholar / arXiv) on the research page; saved papers
  flow into Corpus identically.
- Smoke: `?source=arxiv` search happy-path (XML fetch-fake → arxiv: paper).

entries.heading: Phase 37 — Today's booking → nudge (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Completes the Cal.com integration into the proactive layer: a consulting call later
today surfaces as a Goddess/hub nudge with its discovery brief, linking to bookings.
Read-side (nudges API reads consulting_bookings), no wing edits.

- nudge rule: `upcoming_booking` → "📆 10:00: Discovery call with X — discovery brief ready".
- nudges API gathers the next booking today (start_time ≥ now, ≤ end of SAST day).
- 1 unit test. Full suite **1452/1452**.

entries.heading: Phase 38 — Morning nudge push (mobile reach) (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
The OS now reaches Nanda on her phone. A 07:00 SAST cron computes the day's nudges
and pushes the single highest-priority one (urgent > opportunity) via ntfy.

- **Refactor (test-guarded):** extracted the nudge gathering from the route into
  `src/lib/os/nudge-context.ts` `gatherNudgeContext(supabase, userId)` — shared by the

  the existing nudges smoke test confirmed unchanged behavior.
- `push.nudge` builder (ntfy) added.
- **Cron** `os/nudge-push` (07:00 SAST) — pushes the top urgent/opportunity nudge,
  silent if nothing's worth interrupting for. Registered.

entries.heading: Phase 39 — Dismissable nudges (2026-06-20)
entries.body:
Quality fix: nudges recompute every load and never went away — noisy. Now each can
be snoozed for the rest of the day.

- `POST /api/os/nudges {id}` → redis set `jarvis:nudges:dismissed:{user}:{SAST-date}`
  (24h TTL); GET filters them out. All redis calls defensive (try/catch).
- OS hub: a ✕ snooze button per nudge (optimistic removal + fire-and-forget POST).
- Smoke harness extended to stub `smembers`/`sadd`/`expire`. 3 new smoke tests
  (400 no-id, 200 snooze, GET hides snoozed). Full suite **1455/1455**.

entries.heading: Phase 41 — Graceful-degradation tests (2026-06-20)

failure paths degrade cleanly.

- research GET → 502 when Semantic Scholar is down; → 502 when arXiv is down.
- calcom POST → 200 `{enabled:true, synced:0, reason:"…fetch failed"}` when Cal.com
  is unreachable (never throws).
- Pure test additions (no source change). Full suite **1458/1458**.

entries.session: Phase 50 — Activation, automation revival, wing fixes + video/learning layer (2026-06-29)
entries.heading: Phase 50 — Activation, automation revival, wing fixes + video/learning layer (2026-06-29)
entries.body:

**Stabilisation & activation**
- Killed the `/api/inngest` error flood: removed invalid `betas` param (62 files),
  fixed `.upsert/.insert(...).catch is not a function` (Supabase builder is a thenable,
  no `.catch`) → `.then(ok,err)`, fixed `intelligence_feed` ON CONFLICT (partial unique
  index → dedup-then-insert). 0 errors since. Commit `6e0de0a`.
- Two more 100%-failure causes: `(client).beta.promptCaching.messages.create` (namespace
  removed from the SDK) → `client.messages.create` in dojo-drill + feedback-triage; and
  `JSON.parse()` on Upstash-auto-deserialised Redis signals in emergence-report +
  cross-domain-synthesize. Commit `c62e5b9`.
- Pushed + validated 29 env keys to Vercel (CLI), removed 5 annotation-text placeholders.
  Per-brand Resend wired across all 26 senders. Cloudinary receipt storage. Corpus
  PII-leak fix (record_type-scoped retrieval so CEO/Sanyu private data stops surfacing in
  every wing) + affinity-tag merge + language-tutor grounding. Wordnik dictionary fallback.

**Automation revival** (all 198 workers registered; the gaps were orphan events)
- Revived: `os/eskom-high-stage` consumer (ntfy alert), postmortem-on-incident-resolve,
  sankofa growth-snapshot weekly cron (revives the whole SankofaGrow chain), ux brief on
  suite-create. Created the missing **Habit OS tables**. Removed 3 dead Notion-sync sends.
- **Cross-wing revenue/identity (GAP 1–5):** sanyu shop orders + consulting payments now
  book Finance income (were invisible); delivery→engineering monitoring on launch;
  **unified client_id FK** (consulting_engagements + monitoring_clients → CEO clients);
  new `/api/mirembe/shop-intake`.
- **Golden-brick harvester** (`engineering/golden-brick-harvest`) walks GitHub repos →
  Haiku-extracts → auto-saves. **Service scaffolds** (all 19 Mirembe service types via
  category composition). **Engineer's Dojo guided curriculum** — beginner-first path
  through her stack, AI lesson player + drills + progress.

**Wing fixes + the video/learning layer**
- Cycle: calendar showed a frozen phase → fixed to advance days like /api/cycle/phase;
  predict-next-phase queried a non-existent `date` column (never ran) → `log_date`;
  **real supplement stack + tick-off checklist**; nutrient UTC→SAST fix; **mood/energy
  trend vs gym + workload**.
- Memoir "0/11" tag mismatch fixed. YouTube zero-config channel resolution.
- **Reusable VideoPanel + `/api/video/search`** — Caroline Girvan / combat / dance /
  mind-body (Body, phase-matched in Cycle), full art curriculum (Sanctuary Sketch room).
- Sankofa blessing synced to **moon phase + season + zodiac** of the day.
- Seeded **Persona Council (9)** + **Growth Pillars (7)**. Fixed 3 broken-form endpoints.

**HANDOFF FOR NEXT CHAT** — full open-items list in project memory
`project-wing-fixes-video-session`: 5 missing-route forms (Consulting Reports, Portal
retainer-briefing, Marketing youtube/[id], Finance tax-recalculate + income), remaining
seeds (editorial, platform_registry, os_skills), Inngest now SYNCED (verify crons +
golden-brick harvest fill), GITHUB_TOKEN for private repos, cross-wing fluidity vision.

entries.session: Session 52 — Sanyu launch prep · the video engine · cycle 35-day · UV auto (Jun 30 2026)
entries.heading: Session 52 — Sanyu launch prep · the video engine · cycle 35-day · UV auto (Jun 30 2026)

(R199, 2×200g balm), `combo_luxury_set` (R230, oil+300g) to SKU config + shop-sku-map.

entries.session: Jun 30 2026 (pt 2) — Wing audit + env reconcile + dead-end/stale/sync sweep
entries.heading: Jun 30 2026 (pt 2) — Wing audit + env reconcile + dead-end/stale/sync sweep
entries.body:
**Two-part request:** (1) wing-by-wing review treating each wing as a *living, proactive, self-growing ecosystem*; (2) reconcile `.env.vercel.template` against Vercel prod — "keys with values must be in Vercel, nothing blank."

**Env reconcile (the real bug wasn't missing — it was corrupt).** Vercel CLI was actually installed + authenticated. All 104 value-bearing template keys were already present in prod; nothing blank. But **42 prod env vars were stored with a literal trailing `\n`** (the documented Jun-28 cleanup had never been applied live) — including **`NOTION_TOKEN`**, which is exactly why Notion sync had never run (a corrupted bearer token = every Notion call 401s). Fixed by pulling each var's own value, trimming, and `vercel env add <K> production --force` (printf, no newline) — now stored Sensitive/write-only, verified clean. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://jarvis.mirembemuse.co.za` (the canonical domain; prod held the old vercel.app URL).

**Dead-ends fixed (great plumbing → dead consumer was the systemic pattern):**
- `api/os/signals` GET read `signals:` but the publisher writes `jarvis:signals:` → cache always missed. Same missing-prefix bug in `marketing/weekly-content-gen` cycle read.
- `docs/expiry-check` only returned counts → now inserts expiring docs into `ceo_daily_queue` (deduped per day).
- `marketing/weekly-content-gen` inserted `post_copy:''` + hardcoded `platform:'LinkedIn'` (generated content discarded) → now maps each piece to its real platform + copy.
- New `finance/alert-scan` cron (Mon 08:00 SAST, bias-free rolling-30d windows) fires `finance/alert.check` REVENUE_DIP/BUDGET_SPIKE — nothing fired it before, so the smartest alerts were dead.
- `os/wing-health-monitor` now emits `jarvis/os.overwhelm.check` — the fully-built Mystic overwhelm responder had no producer (was unreachable).
- Task + todo completion now `awardXP('os.task_complete')` (new catalog action) — completion gave no XP despite XP being wired into 30 wings.
- LCL dead-ends: `goddess_sessions`, `video_progress`, `email_inbound` now feed `lib/os/living-context.ts` (graceful-degradation guarded) so captured intelligence reaches the AI context.

**Stales:** Sanyu First-Batch prices R130(oil50)/R145(balm200)/R189(balm300) corrected in `competitor-snapshot`, `weekly-profitability`, `reorder-planner` (+ fixed the stale `SANYU-BALM-125` SKU reads that always returned 0). Source of truth = `SANYU_SKU_CONFIG`.

**Mismatches:** `scholar/fragment-resonance` cast referenced undefined `sonnet` → `haiku`; `cycle/predict-next-phase` 7-day fallback → 35-day PHASE_DEFAULTS (her real cycle). Found+fixed a pre-existing bug: `created()` was imported by 8 POST routes but never exported from `api-response.ts` (every create 500'd) → added the export.

**Notion — no-gaps sync sweep.** Root cause (corrupt token) fixed above. Then made every wing's sync helper **idempotent**: consulting/autobiography/body/docs/sanctuary/sankofa/ux/sanyu-order helpers now `pages.update` the existing page instead of creating duplicates (workers already wrote `notion_page_id` back; finance + sanyu batch/inventory were already idempotent). Forwarded `notion_page_id` in the sanyu-order worker. Cross-checked: every `NOTION_DB_*` the code reads exists in prod (only `NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID` absent — and it's only used inside an Engineering *scaffold template* for other projects, not JarvisOS sync). Added `scripts/verify-notion-all.mjs` to confirm DB-sharing + live property schemas across every DB.

**Infra:** `package.json` engines → `node: 24.x` (Vercel deprecates Node 20 builds from Oct 1 2026).

**Agent claims corrected during audit:** `engineering/postmortem-generate` is fully implemented (not a placeholder); `os/overwhelm-detection` was complete (only its trigger was missing).

**Deploy topology gotcha:** the `.vercel` link lives in the OUTER `JarvisOS/` but the Next app + git repo are the INNER `JarvisOS/JarvisOS/`. `vercel --prod` from the outer dir fails ("No Next.js at root"); must copy `.vercel/project.json` into the inner dir and deploy from there. Build runs with `Skipping validation of types`, so import/export correctness (not TS) is what matters at runtime.

entries.session: Jun 30 – Jul 2 2026 — The Payment Epic: unified PayFast hub → multi-app → Paystack subscriptions
entries.heading: Jun 30 – Jul 2 2026 — The Payment Epic: unified PayFast hub → multi-app → Paystack subscriptions
entries.body:
Multi-day arc that took the whole revenue empire from fragmented/unwired to a live, reliable, provider-agnostic payment system. See memory: `project-payfast-unified`, `project-payfast-multiapp`, `project-paystack-subscriptions`.

**Keys activated + OAuth live (Jun 30).** Pushed Google/Vercel/GitHub/Notion keys to Vercel via REST API (CLI not installed that session), redeployed. **Gmail + Calendar OAuth now LINKED** — critical gotcha: the OAuth app must be **published to Production** in Google Cloud or refresh tokens die in 7 days (Testing mode). **Inngest synced** (`PUT /api/inngest` → modified:true) — unblocked the orphaned golden-brick harvester + eskom-high-stage worker; fired the harvester (golden_bricks 0→16+, real TS patterns).

**PayFast unified hub (Jun 30).** Root bug: the 4 PayFast touchpoints used **3 different signature algorithms** (two sorted params alphabetically → would silently REJECT real ITNs). Built ONE canonical engine `src/lib/payfast/core.ts` (form-order signature, PHP urlencode, sandbox-first) + ONE ITN endpoint `/api/payfast/notify` (validate once, log to `payfast_itn_log`, idempotent via a **unique index on transactions.payfast_payment_id**, route by `mm.<app>.<kind>.<ref>` codec). Migration `payfast_unified_foundation` added `subscriptions` + `payfast_itn_log` + the index. Aliased the 3 legacy routes to the canonical handler. Verified offline (`scripts/payfast-verify.mts`). **Live R5 test** exposed the ITN gotcha: PayFast's ITN signature **INCLUDES empty fields** (unlike the payment request which excludes them) — reproduced PayFast's exact MD5 to prove it, fixed `verifySignature` (includeEmpty=true), locked with a regression test using the real ITN vector. Also fixed: prod `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` was still the dead `creativelynanda.co.za` → payments' notify_url pointed nowhere (repointed to jarvis.mirembemuse.co.za).

**Multi-app unification (Jun 30).** Decision: ONE Mirembe merchant (17030173) for everything. Cloned the 4 app repos (via GITHUB_TOKEN). Hub upgraded to book **central Finance for every app** (one revenue stream per business) + forward the verified ITN to each app's real receiver. Wired VarsityOS/AdminOS/K53/Sanyu (checkout → hub + `mm.<app>.*` id; receiver trusts `x-hub-secret`). **Found+fixed the alphabetical-ksort signature bug in VarsityOS + K53.** **⚠️ GIT LESSON:** Windows `git clone --depth 1` of campus-compass + sanyu checked out incompletely (case-collisions) → left staged deletions in the index → `git add <files>; git commit` (no pathspec) swept **727 / 388 file deletions** into the commits → builds failed (never deployed, prod safe). Recovered: force-pushed the good parent, then re-applied edits via the **GitHub Contents API**. RULE: edit these external repos via the GitHub API, not Windows clones.

**K53 free-premium (critical security fix, Jun 30).** `verify.js`/`claim.js` honoured the checkout unlock token (minted pre-payment) on its own → anyone went pro without paying. Compounded by K53 storing its Supabase URL as `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` (code read unset `SUPABASE_URL` → threw, masked as "Parse error" → the subscribers path never worked, so the token was the only grant). Fixed: token carries the m_payment_id ref; ITN stores it on the subscriber; verify/claim now REQUIRE a matching ITN-confirmed subscriber; app retries verify ~30s for the redirect-vs-ITN race; all fns fall back to VITE_SUPABASE_URL. Proven: unconfirmed token → `{pending:true}`.

**PayFast subscriptions failed → pivot to Paystack (Jul 2).** VarsityOS/AdminOS/K53-monthly subscriptions kept failing at the PayFast payment page (403 then a generic 500 "Server Error" page). Proved it's NOT our code — submitted VarsityOS's exact subscription request 5 ways, all accepted (302); `status.payfast.io` API showed **"Partially Degraded Service"** (their General component degraded). PayFast's recurring billing has been unreliable for months. **Decision: PayFast = one-time (Sanyu, Mirembe products), Paystack = subscriptions.** Also found+fixed AdminOS sending `billing_date` (PayFast 400s on it).

**Paystack subscriptions (Jul 2, PROVEN + wired).** Built `src/lib/paystack/core.ts` (HMAC-SHA512 webhook verify, initSubscription, createPlan, getSubscription/getTransactionById, reference codec) + `/api/paystack/webhook` hub (books central Finance on charge.success AND subscription.create — fetches the subscription's numeric invoice.transaction id → resolves to the reference so both flows share one idempotency key) + `/api/paystack/checkout` (per-app `plan/email/ref/callback`). Created 8 Plans via API. **Full loop PROVEN in test**: K53 R29 subscription → webhook → central Finance (R29 income, source=k53drillmaster) → active subscription → Revenue Streams dashboard shows **MRR R29 / ARR R348 / 1 active sub**. Gotcha fixed: `transactions_category_check` didn't allow `'subscription'` (migration `transactions_add_subscription_category`) — this also unblocked PayFast-hub subscription bookings. Then **wired all 3 apps** to Paystack (VarsityOS `initiate`+receiver, AdminOS `billing/checkout` plans + receiver, K53 monthly → Paystack hosted page + email-based receiver), each with prominent "⚠️ DO NOT REVERT TO PAYFAST" notes — all deployed green.

**Finance multi-stream + net-profit fix (Jun 30 / Jul 2).** New `/api/finance/streams` + `/dashboard/finance/streams` (income per business + MRR/ARR). Fixed the headline Net Profit that only showed month-to-date (July=R29) → now shows **all-time** (R3,479.64 = R9,529 income − R6,049 expenses) with this-month + totals underneath.

**Sanyu (Jul 2).** Reconciled the website↔JarvisOS handshake secrets on BOTH Vercel projects (`SANYU_OS_API_KEY`=`SANYU_SHOP_ORDER_SECRET` for orders; `JARVIS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`=`SANYU_SHOP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for stock-sync). Removed the too-long product LifecycleFeed from the dashboard. Site live (200).

**OPEN:** Pargo delivery + pickup-point address directory in Sanyu (blocked on the Pargo API key — user getting it). Paystack GO-LIVE = swap test→live keys, recreate the 8 plans in live mode, register the live webhook URL. AdminOS add-ons still need Paystack plans. Security note given to user: do NOT centralise all apps' Supabase service-role keys in the shared template (blast radius; each app owns its own key in its own Vercel project).

---

entries.session: Jul 3 2026 — Live-testing wing sweep (CEO email → Marketing → Engineering → UX → Consulting → Scholar) + AI-cost self-logging + k6 + the dead-cron discovery
entries.heading: Jul 3 2026 — Live-testing wing sweep (CEO email → Marketing → Engineering → UX → Consulting → Scholar) + AI-cost self-logging + k6 + the dead-cron discovery
entries.body:
Wing-by-wing from Nanda's live testing. 10 commits on master (`091a463`→`452cbb4`); memory: `project-wing-sweep-jul3`. The systemic Engineering bug this session was **pages reading `json.data.<wrong-key>`** — great routes, wrong consumer key.

**CEO Email — the flagship "make it super advanced + mobile".** Gmail showed but was a dead list. Rebuilt: new `GET /api/email/gmail/message/[id]` + `getGmailMessage()` (walks the payload tree for text/html, marks read, returns the RFC Message-ID) → messages are now **clickable to full body** with **threaded reply/forward/search**; page rebuilt **mobile-first** as a master-detail with a back-button overlay (was a cramped desktop 2-panel on phones). Fixed a real send bug: the composer offered all 5 domains but `send/route.ts` enum only accepted 3 (varsityos/adminos/sanyubotanicals would 422), and "Gmail" was wrongly routed through Resend (can't send from an unverified gmail.com) → now accepts all 5 registry domains + routes the `gmail` account through the Gmail API. That's "wire all the other emails" on the send side (inbound receive still needs Resend inbound routing in their dashboard).

**Sanctuary hero** was a near-black empty band — the painting is intentionally CSS-disabled (`globals.css` prior user pref). Turned the dead gradient into a designed violet **nebula** (layered radial glows) so it reads as an intentional cosmic hero, not blank.

**Marketing (4 fixes).** *Editorial* was always empty from a `data.strategies` vs `data.editorial` key mismatch — the 11 brands were seeded the whole time. *Approval* "black screen" = a full-viewport `#0A0A0A` wrapper + **headerless fetches** (401 → empty) → normal wing shell + auth headers. *Content bank 404* → built the missing `content-bank/page.tsx` (its API + 44 seeded rows already existed). *Brand portfolios* only read (empty) `brand_posts` → now also render a **Brand DNA** card from `brand_editorial` (voice, pillars, aesthetic, typography, cadence, colour-palette swatches, best platforms, faceless persona).

**Engineering (the wrong-key sweep).** *NOC* queried non-existent `monitored_apps.user_id` (real col `owner_user_id`) AND filtered `deleted_at` (no such column) → fixed to `owner_user_id` + `active`. *Tech Radar* read `data.[ring]` instead of `data.byRing`/`items`; its AI-update + ring-change buttons sent payloads the route didn't accept (`trigger_update`, `technology`). *AI Lab* — all 3 tabs mismatched: costs `data.costs`→`by_group`, prompts→`items`, prompt-test/rag-health request+response keys aligned to the routes. *Evolution* alerts filter used `'alert'` vs stream key `'alerts'` (could never toggle off). *Load Testing* read `data.tests`→`items` + normalised the table's `run_at/error_rate_pct/max_rps` to the UI shape. Verified live under tenant `8a090028`: tech_radar=22, prompts=29 — so these now show real data, not empty.

**UX "doesn't make sense" → two clean zones (user picked "both, cleanly split").** It had three colour identities (amber root / red brand pages / rainbow banner) and bundled three unrelated jobs. Unified to **one RED `#F87171`** identity across root + `WingHero` + `WingBanner` (🌈→🎨), restructured the root into **"Your Design System"** (Format Templates, Palette Tokens, App Coherence Monitor) and **"Client Brand Work"** (Brand Systems, Client Visual Suites), and surfaced the orphaned Brands page in the wing nav.

**Consulting — "not editable" + "theme it like Notion".** New `PATCH /api/consulting/proposals/[id]` (there was none) → proposals now **Edit** + **"Mark as Sent"** (the missing draft→sent transition that made Accept unreachable) + Mark Declined. Engagement detail got an **Edit modal** for its own fields (client/value/dates/notes) — the PATCH route already accepted them; the UI just never exposed it. Fixed a latent bug: notes live in the `description` column but the page read a nonexistent `notes`. Then **reskinned** the three legacy slate pages (engagements list, engagement detail, board) from the old `bg-slate-800`/violet era to the standard indigo wing shell.

**Scholar — "is it where it should be?"** Confirmed genuinely vast (17 pages, 37 routes). The only gap: 3 elite tracks (Law/China/High-Stakes) were backend-live (`law-chat`, `i-ching`, `book-practice`, elite briefs + an `intelligence-elite` page) but unlinked from the dashboard → surfaced them as tracks and retargeted the weak Legal link to the real elite page.

**AI Lab now actually tracks (self-logging).** The Cost Observatory had no data source (Helicone never integrated). Rather than touch dozens of call sites, wrapped `client.messages.create` **and** `messages.stream` (via the `finalMessage` event) inside `buildClient()` in `anthropic.ts` → **every** Anthropic call auto-logs model/tokens/cost/latency to `engineering_ai_costs` (`src/lib/ai/cost-log.ts`, fire-and-forget, never blocks). Streaming rows log with null wing (deferred); wing-chat opening messages attribute their wing. Populates on next deploy + any AI usage.

**Load Testing — built the missing k6 workflow.** The trigger fired a `repository_dispatch` into the void — no workflow existed to catch it. Added `.github/workflows/k6-load-test.yml`: installs k6, runs the scenario against `https://<app>.co.za`, extracts p50/p95/p99/error-rate/RPS/iterations via `handleSummary`, POSTs to `/api/engineering/load-tests/results` with `INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. End-to-end wired; go-live needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` + the matching secret (user config).

**NOC "show data now" → uncovered a dead cron.** Seeded/confirmed 9 `monitored_apps` (7 lowercase-slug apps pre-existed; added Sanyu + Mirembe). Triggered `POST /api/engineering/health` (fires `engineering/health.check`; `inngest.send` returned queued:true) — but **zero new rows appeared**. Investigation: `app_health_checks` has 20,503 rows but the last automated one was **Jun 29** — the health cron (and `world_feed`/`scholar_intelligence_feed`, both null) has been **dead ~4 days**. Code side is *correct* (`engineeringHealthCheck` is imported + in the `functions` array + served); and the service-role admin path works in prod (the health GET returned data) — so it's an **Inngest Cloud sync/execution regression**, almost certainly from the Jun 29–30 key pushes (stale sync against an old deploy URL, or `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`/`EVENT_KEY` mismatch). As a stopgap, ran real HTTP pings myself and inserted 9 live rows → **NOC shows data now** (6 up; stokvelos degraded/404; watchsankofa + sankofasessions down/unreachable). HANDOFF (user, app.inngest.com): confirm the app is synced to the current prod URL, verify signing/event keys match Vercel, check for a paused app / failed runs, ensure the Vercel↔Inngest integration auto-syncs on deploy — that revives health + all crons and NOC's 15-min auto-refresh.

**Still needs user config (no code left):** `GITHUB_TOKEN` in Vercel → lights up Load Testing (dispatch; workflow now exists) + Workflow Intelligence (analyzes commits via GitHub API — token only); `INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` matched (Vercel + GH secret) for k6 callback; Resend inbound routing to *receive* the 5 domains; the Inngest re-sync above. `brand_posts` stays unseeded (posts appear as created/generated — not faked).

entries.session: Jul 3 2026 (night) — 🎉 PAYSTACK WENT LIVE: first real subscription, lifecycle, backbone enshrined
entries.heading: Jul 3 2026 (night) — 🎉 PAYSTACK WENT LIVE: first real subscription, lifecycle, backbone enshrined
entries.ownerQuote: this is the backbone of all future apps
entries.body:
The night the empire started earning. Paystack account **approved & live**, and by end of night a **real R89/month VarsityOS Nova subscription** had flowed the whole loop — payment → webhook → central Finance → active sub → MRR. Memory: `project-paystack-subscriptions`.

**Go-live was pure ops — zero code (as designed).** The engine auto-detects live from the `sk_live_` prefix and pulls every plan code from env, so going live never needed a redeploy of logic. Grabbed the `sk_live_`/`pk_live_` keys, ran `scripts/paystack-golive.mjs` (loading the live key inline from the outer template so the secret never entered the chat context) → created all **8 LIVE Plans** clean-slate (VarsityOS Scholar R29 / Nova R89, K53 R29, AdminOS Solo R349 / Grow R899 / Operate R1999 / Scale R3999 / Partner R9999). Found `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` already in the template → pushed all **10 live Paystack vars** (secret + public + 8 plan codes) into the `jarvis-os` **Production** env via REST API and redeployed — Vercel driven fully headless from here. Created the **K53 live hosted payment page** (`/page` API rejects the `PLN_` code — must pass the plan's *numeric* id) → `paystack.com/pay/r2t57b3pt9`, pushed its full URL to the K53 Vercel project. All 8 plans + the K53 page LIVE.

**Subscription lifecycle + the plan-code drift kill (commit `bcab6e1`).** Root-caused a live bug before it could bite: the webhook's `PLAN_APP` map and the cancel route's plan list were **hardcoded TEST plan codes** → in live mode cancel would always 404, and K53 hosted-page subs (`subscription.create` with no app metadata → attribution falls to the plan code) would resolve to `unknown` and never activate the buyer. Fix: `core.ts` now derives **both** maps from the `PAYSTACK_PLAN_*` env vars — the *same* codes checkout redirects against — via `planCodeToApp()` / `appToPlanCodes(app)`, so they can never drift again when plans are recreated. Added three hub routes, all gated by `x-hub-secret === HUB_INTERNAL_SECRET` with **Paystack as source of truth** and each scoped to only the requesting app's own plans: `POST /api/paystack/cancel` (customer → getSubscription → email_token → disableSubscription), `POST /api/paystack/reactivate` (enable a `non-renewing` sub; 409 `action:'checkout'` if fully lapsed), `GET /api/paystack/subscription?email=&app=` (status list for a Manage view). Verified live: 403 without secret, 400 on bad input, 200 empty list, checkout still 302.

**Backbone locked into the Golden Bricks (commit `78b9384`).** At Nanda's request — "this is the backbone of all future apps" — enshrined the proven loop in `src/data/golden-bricks.json` (seeded live via `scripts/seed-golden-bricks.mjs`, +2 bricks): (1) **"Paystack subscription engine"** — full engine incl. cancel/reactivate + the drift-proof env-derived plan-code maps; (2) **"Paystack webhook hub — the money loop"** — verify → resolveApp (metadata → reference → plan-code) → **idempotent** central-Finance booking (a unique index on the reference turns a replayed webhook into a swallowed 23505 → never double-counts) → enqueue for the Finance/MRR rollup → forward the raw event to the owning app. Both the app-init `charge.success` and hosted-page `subscription.create` flows. Gotcha logged: the seed **upserts by (user_id, title) with no prune** — renaming a brick orphans the old row (had to delete the stale old-title one by hand). Every future subscription app now inherits this verbatim.

**App cancel buttons — all 3 wired + deployed.** Each app's UI cancel → its own backend route (email ALWAYS derived server-side from the session, never client-supplied) → hub `/api/paystack/cancel`. **K53** (`2043a0a`): `api/cancel.js` existed uncommitted; rendered the missing Cancel button + confirm flow into `Settings.jsx` "Your Plan" (gated `!isNative()` — native uses Play billing). **AdminOS** (`35878bb`): built `app/api/billing/cancel/route.ts` (Supabase session + `checkPermission('manage_billing')`) + a client `CancelSubscriptionButton` wired into the billing Current-plan card (only when `!isOnTrial && sub`). **VarsityOS** was **already fully wired** in the real repo — and re-confirmed the **clone trap**: the local `campus-compass` working copy is stale/broken (whole tree untracked, still showing old PayFast routes), while GitHub `main` has the correct Paystack cancel route + `ProfileClient` button. Rule reinforced: inspect/edit campus-compass via the GitHub API, never the local clone.

**Git credentials secured.** All three app remotes had a GitHub PAT embedded in the `.git/config` URL (`x-access-token:…@`). Stripped them to clean `https://github.com/…` URLs and let auth flow through **Git Credential Manager** (already the system-level helper → Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI-encrypted); `ls-remote` verified on all three post-cleanup. Updated the AdminOS remote to its canonical `Nanda-Regine/AdminOS.git`. User is rotating the leaked PAT (first push after rotation re-auths GCM via browser once, then resumes).

**🥂 THE FIRST REAL SALE.** Nanda subscribed in VarsityOS with a live card. Confirmed in the central hub DB seconds later: `transactions` → **R89 income, source `varsityos`, category `subscription`**, ref `mm.varsityos.subscription.5cfce67e…` (the `charge.success` app-init flow, idempotent key); `subscriptions` → **varsityos · ACTIVE · R89/monthly · nandaregine@gmail.com**.
